claim: The paper is classified as small.
problem: Supported status: needs clarification (clarify). Random assignment of AI configurations and a sample below 50 are established, but an output-scored comparison of those randomized configurations is not. The sole creativity result is a qualitative assessment pooled across teams, with no reported arm-specific scores or comparison. The form marks the output criterion met without establishing the required randomized-arm outcome; whether such a comparison exists needs clarification.
evidence: report-data.json: status_by_cid.c898 = small. forms/c898.json: eligibility.criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output = met, but studies[0].outcomes[0].contrasts[0] has empty treatment_arm, control_arm and comparison_type; its reported field explicitly states that no numerical creativity scores, arm-specific results or statistical contrast between AI configurations are reported. Independently checked the complete PDF at retrieval.json[c898].pdf_path, Sattele and Ortiz (2025) - AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams.pdf. PDF p. 3 (printed 411), Section 3.1 reports 19 students; PDF p. 4 (printed 412), Section 3.3 reports random assignment of tools. Section 4 on that page describes CAT evaluation by two experts and calls the solutions obvious and generic; the remaining Results and Discussion (PDF pp. 5-9) provide qualitative observations, not scores comparing the randomized configurations.

claim: The paper is classified as small.
problem: Supported status: needs clarification (clarify). The form explicitly leaves the creativity-output criterion unclear, with no final resolution. Its scored design-performance rubric measures visual communication, while creative self-efficacy is self-reported. The below-50 sample does not settle whether that rubric supplies an eligible creativity outcome. The unresolved outcome criterion should not be treated as satisfied when assigning small status.
